title: Incremental OSHA Forms 300/301 electronic submission: deprioritized on agency cost estimate

history.reason: Initial rejection rationale (superseded in scope below): OSHA estimates about $136 per year per affected establishment; the earlier inference that 100+ employee establishments cannot be small businesses was incorrect.

Review correction: rejected only the incremental Forms 300/301 submission thesis on the limited agency estimate, not broader OSHA reporting/recordkeeping. SBA-small entities can have 100+ employees; existing Form 300A reporting covers some establishments with 20+ employees.

description: Discovery of the 2023 rule’s incremental annual electronic submission of Forms 300 and 301 by establishments with 100 or more employees in designated industries. Deprioritized as a research thesis using OSHA’s modeled added cost, without claiming that all OSHA reporting or recordkeeping is inexpensive.
customer_segment: Establishments with 100+ employees in OSHA-designated industries, including some SBA-defined small entities. Establishment employee count is not a firm-size classification.
context: Historical July 2023 rule analysis, narrowly about added Forms 300/301 electronic submission. It does not evaluate existing Form 300A submissions for certain establishments with 20+ employees or total recordkeeping burden. Later rule status was not established.

evidence.text: For the 2023 rule’s added Forms 300/301 electronic submission, OSHA estimates average annual cost of $136 per affected establishment (annualized over 10 years at 7%); this is not total OSHA recordkeeping cost.
Only establishments with 100 or more employees in designated industries are required to submit Forms 300 and 301 electronically.
OSHA states the information submitted is already required to be kept.
The rule discusses affected SBA-defined small entities; it also preserves existing Form 300A electronic submission requirements for certain establishments with 20 or more employees.

alternatives: Manual entry through OSHA's submission portal; existing safety-management software: not investigated.

contradictory_evidence.text: The agency’s modeled incremental submission cost is low relative to the generic automation thesis; this is a research-priority judgment, not measured customer burden. Independent higher-cost evidence was not obtained.

uncertainty: Unknown: actual incremental submission time, SBA-small firm distribution, error/penalty exposure, total recordkeeping burden, and later regulatory changes. The $136 modeled average does not establish any individual employer’s cost.
open_questions: Is the underlying injury recordkeeping process, rather than submission, the pain point?
next_actions: Reopen this narrow submission thesis with independent evidence of material residual cost or errors.
Treat any broader Form 300A or underlying recordkeeping problem as separate research with its own evidence.
